properties.displayName: [WEEKLY] Internet-Facing Service Daemon Spawns Shell or Ingress Tool Then Beacons Out
properties.description:
Detects a long-running, internet-exposed service daemon (java/TeamCity agent, node/MCP-bridge, gitea/git, uhttpd/LuCI, nginx/php, python) spawning an OS command interpreter or ingress-transfer binary (sh/bash/cmd/powershell/curl/wget/certutil/bitsadmin/nc) and then making an outbound connection to a public IP within a 5-minute window — the post-exploitation signature shared by this fortnight's unauthenticated-RCE wave. It matters now because six critical (CVSS 9.8-10.0) flaws all landed together: CVE-2026-53921 OpenWrt DHCPv6/LuCI root RCE ('Critical OpenWrt DHCPv6 Flaw…'), CVE-2026-63077 TeamCity unauth OS command exec ('Critical TeamCity Flaw…'), CVE-2026-60004 Gitea git-hook RCE ('New Gitea RCE Lets Repository Writers Plant a Git Hook…'), CVE-2026-59726 Ruflo MCP RufRoot RCE ('Ruflo MCP Flaw Lets Unauthenticated Attackers Run Commands…'), the DEV#POPPER @joyfill npm RAT ('Two Compromised joyfill npm Packages…'), and CVE-2026-67426 Flyto2 SSRF ('Flyto2 Core… callback_url SSRF'). Every IOC in those advisories rotates, but the daemon→shell→egress chain persists, so the UC keys on the process-lineage TTP rather than any hash or C2 host. It spans the exploit → execution → command-and-control kill-chain stages by requiring the server-parent/shell-child pairing AND a subsequent public egress. It FIRES when a web/app service account's process tree pivots to an interactive shell or downloader that then dials out; it does NOT fire on developer or CI shells launched by a human logon, on daemon-to-daemon internal traffic with no shell spawn, or on a shell spawn with no outbound follow-through.

Rationale: Every article describes a different unauthenticated RCE, but the shared observable is an internet-exposed service process pivoting to an OS shell/downloader and then reaching out — this UC keys on that parent-daemon→shell-child→public-egress lineage instead of the per-CVE IOCs that rotate weekly.
properties.query:
let Window = 5m;
let Daemons = dynamic(["java.exe","java","node.exe","node","gitea","git.exe","git","httpd.exe","nginx.exe","w3wp.exe","php-cgi.exe","php.exe","python.exe","python3","uhttpd","dnsmasq","tomcat.exe"]);
let Shells = dynamic(["cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","sh","bash","dash","zsh","curl.exe","wget.exe","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe","nc.exe","ncat.exe"]);
let SpawnEvents = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any (Daemons)
    | where FileName has_any (Shells)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project SpawnTime = TimeGenerated, DeviceId, DeviceName, AccountName,
              ParentProc = InitiatingProcessFileName, ChildProc = FileName,
              ChildCmd = ProcessCommandLine;
SpawnEvents
| join kind=inner (
    DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where RemoteIPType == "Public"
    | project NetTime = TimeGenerated, DeviceId, RemoteIP, RemotePort,
              NetProc = InitiatingProcessFileName
  ) on DeviceId
| where NetTime between (SpawnTime .. SpawnTime + Window)
| project SpawnTime, NetTime,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', NetTime, SpawnTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, ParentProc, ChildProc, ChildCmd,
          RemoteIP, RemotePort, NetProc
| order by SpawnTime desc
